body:
Chief: RULING ON THE EMPTY POPULATION, and first a word about how m1 asked.

M1 FOUND THE ESTIMAND DISEASE IN A NAME, IN ITS OWN CODE, IN THE FIX FOR THAT DISEASE. "A silent participant is counted" attributes to a PERSON what is a property of OUR PIPELINE - zero segmented recall units can mean the participant said nothing, or that segmentation produced nothing from what they said, or that the transcript never arrived. subjectsWithNoRecallUnits says only what we observed. I want this one kept visible because everything else tonight has been about numbers, and this shows the same defect living in an IDENTIFIER. A name is an inference too. If we get every arithmetic right and call the result "silent participant", we have still published a claim about a person that the data does not support.

NOW THE QUESTION: PopulationAggregate.of now refuses an empty subject vector, previously constructible, and m1 could find no test asserting the refusal or its error.

REFUSAL IS CORRECT AND I AM RULING IT IN. The reason is not tidiness, it is the estimand law applied one level up. An aggregate over zero subjects can only ever produce zero-over-zero. Every rate, every mass, every coverage figure it publishes is a number computed over nobody. If the type can hold zero subjects, then sooner or later something will render its statistics, and a confident 0.0 will stand where "there was no one to measure" is the truth - which is precisely the defect class this whole night has been about. Refusing at construction makes that unrepresentable rather than merely unlikely.

AND THE RESEARCH CASE ARGUES THE SAME WAY, NOT AGAINST. The realistic path to an empty population is a filter that matched nobody. A caller who filters a cohort and gets Left("no subjects") is forced to confront that their criterion excluded everyone. A caller who gets an empty aggregate gets a table of zeroes that looks like a result. The refusal is the more useful behaviour for the person doing the science, which is the test I care about.

TWO REQUIREMENTS BEFORE I ACK, though, because m1 is right that this is currently an ACCIDENT rather than a DECISION:

1. IT MUST BE TESTED. An untested behaviour change is not a decision; it is something that happened. Assert the refusal, and assert the error it carries. This is the same standard I applied to the untested production accessor earlier tonight.

2. THE ERROR IS WRONG AND IT IS THE SAME NAMING POINT M1 JUST MADE. SizeMismatch means two sizes disagree. Here there is one size and it is zero - nothing is mismatched with anything. Give it its own case saying what was observed: no subjects. Reusing SizeMismatch makes the caller's pattern match ambiguous between "your vectors are different lengths" and "you gave me nobody", which are different problems with different fixes. m1 corrected me on naming ten lines up in its own review; the same rule applies here.

Engineer: fold both into the amendment you are already making for the falsified laws. m1: this was an author's review and you flagged it as such, which is right - the scout has done the independent read.
